question.problem: Because of network congestion, a computer successfully loads a web page with an $18%$ chance on each attempt. The page is repeatedly reloaded until it successfully loads. Rounded to $3$ decimal places, the probability that it will take exactly $7$ attempts is{{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
A geometric random variable $X$ with probability of success $p$ has the following probability mass function:

$$
f(x)=(1-p)^{x-1}p
$$

Let $X$ be the number of attempts made until the page successfully loads. Since the chance of successfully loading the page is $18%,$ the number of attempts until the page successfully loads can be modeled as a geometric random variable with a probability of success

$$
p=18%=\frac{18}{100}=0.18.
$$

So, $X∼\text{Geom}(0.18).$ In this case, $X$ has the following probability mass function:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =(1-0.18)^{x-1}(0.18) \\  & =(0.82)^{x-1}(0.18)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the probability that the page will successfully load for the first time on the $7$th attempt is

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X=7) & =f(7) \\  & =(0.82)^{7-1}(0.18) \\  & =(0.82)^{6}(0.18) \\  & ≈0.055,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $3$ decimal places.
